messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Tamil, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------| | **Nel** | “in the middle of” – locative prepositional phrase introducing the central point | Use locative case (‑இல்) on the Tamil equivalent of *mezzo*; ensure the phrase precedes the temporal noun. **Back‑translation:** “Midway” | | **mezzo** | “the central point of a span; here the midpoint of life’s journey” | Translate as **மத்திய** (mid) with locative suffix ‑இல் (மத்தியஇல்). Must agree in number (singular) and gender (neutral). **Back‑translation:** “midway” | | **del** | Genitive linking “road” to “our life” | Render the genitive relationship with the Tamil post‑position **உடைய** or the possessive suffix **‑து** after *வாழ்க்கை* (life). **Back‑translation:** “of” | | **cammin** | “the route or way that one travels on; metaphor for life’s course” | Translate as **வழி** (road) in the nominative; no inflection needed beyond the genitive link to *வாழ்க்கை*. **Back‑translation:** “road” | | **di** | Marks possession/association between “road” and “our life” | Use the Tamil genitive marker **‑இன்** attached to *வாழ்க்கை* (வாழ்க்கையின்). **Back‑translation:** “of” | | **nostra** | “belonging to the speaker and companions; collective ownership of life” | Render as the possessive adjective **எங்கள்** (our) agreeing in number (plural) and case (genitive) with *வாழ்க்கை*. **Back‑translation:** “our” | | **vita** | “the span of existence of the speaker; the overall journey” | Translate as **வாழ்க்கை** (life) in the genitive case (**வாழ்க்கையின்**) to link with *வழி*. **Back‑translation:** “life” | | **mi** | Reflexive pronoun, 1st‑person singular (subject/object) | Use the reflexive pronoun **என்னை** as the object of *கண்டுபிடித்தேன்*; subject is implicit in the verb. **Back‑translation:** “myself” | | **ritrovai** | “the act of discovering or realizing one’s own state” | Render with past tense, perfective aspect verb **கண்டுபிடித்தேன்** (I found). Must agree with 1st‑person singular subject. **Back‑translation:** “found” | | **per** | Preposition “through, within” indicating interior location | Use the locative post‑position **உள்ளில்** after *ஒரு* (a) + *காடு* (forest). **Back‑translation:** “within” | | **una** | Indefinite article “a” (non‑specific noun) | Translate as **ஒரு** (a) preceding *காடு*. No case marking needed. **Back‑translation:** “a” | | **selva** | “a densely wooded area; metaphorically dark and confusing” | Translate as **காடு** (forest/wood) in the locative case (**காட்டில்**) due to *per*. **Back‑translation:** “wood” | | **oscura** | “lacking light; conveys gloom and uncertainty” | Use adjective **இருண்ட** (dark) agreeing in gender (feminine) and number (singular) with *காடு*; placed before the noun or after with a copula as per Tamil style. **Back‑translation:** “dark” | | **ché** | Conjunction “because, for” introducing a causal clause | Render with causal conjunction **ஏனெனில்** (because). Must precede the clause. **Back‑translation:** “for” | | **la** | Definite article specifying the particular way | Tamil does not use articles; omit but ensure the noun *வழி* is definite by context. **Back‑translation:** “the” | | **diritta** | “correct or proper; the morally/technically correct path” | Translate as **சரியான** (right/correct) agreeing with *வழி* (feminine singular). **Back‑translation:** “right” | | **via** | “the correct route or method of proceeding” | Translate as **வழி** (way) in nominative; takes the adjective *சரியான*. **Back‑translation:** “way” | | **era** | Past state of being, auxiliary for passive construction | Use imperfect past of *இருக்கிறது* → **இருந்தது** (was). Must agree with singular feminine subject *வழி*. **Back‑translation:** “had been” | | **smarrita** | “the state of being lost or not found; the correct way is absent” | Render as past participle **இழந்த** (lost) used adjectivally with *வழி*; combined with *இருந்தது* to form passive sense: **இழந்தது**. **Back‑translation:** “missed” |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Tamil components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 1: எங்கள் வாழ்க்கையின் பாதையின் நடுவில் / எங்கள் வாழ்க்கையின் மத்திய பாதையில் / எங்கள் வாழ்க்கையின் பாதையின் மத்தியில் - Line 2: நான் ஒரு இருண்ட காடில் என்னை கண்டுபிடித்தேன் / என்னை ஒரு இருண்ட காடில் கண்டுபிடித்தேன் / ஒரு இருண்ட காடில் நான் என்னை கண்டுபிடித்தேன் - Line 3: ஏனெனில் சரியான வழி இழந்திருந்தது / ஏனென்றால் சரியான வழி இழந்திருந்தது / அதனால் சரியான வழி இழந்திருந்தது

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Tamil lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

Source Line: 1 Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita Line Inventory: - எங்கள் வாழ்க்கையின் பாதையின் நடுவில் Assembly Notes: - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase itself expresses the locative meaning. Target Text: எங்கள் வாழ்க்கையின் பாதையின் நடுவில்
Source Line: 2 mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, Line Inventory: - நான் ஒரு இருண்ட காடில் என்னை கண்டுபிடித்தேன் Assembly Notes: - No extra morphology required; the phrase already contains subject, object and locative. Target Text: நான் ஒரு இருண்ட காடில் என்னை கண்டுபிடித்தேன்,
Source Line: 3 ché la diritta via era smarrita. Line Inventory: - ஏனெனில் சரியான வழி இழந்திருந்தது Assembly Notes: - No extra linking needed; the causal conjunction “ஏனெனில்” directly introduces the clause. Target Text: ஏனெனில் சரியான வழி இழந்திருந்தது.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Tamil text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 1 - Target Text (from Step 4): எங்கள் வாழ்க்கையின் பாதையின் நடுவில் - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): in the middle of our life's path - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): Midway upon the road of our life - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 2 - Target Text (from Step 4): நான் ஒரு இருண்ட காடில் என்னை கண்டுபிடித்தேன், - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): I found myself in a dark forest - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): I found myself within a dark wood, - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 3 - Target Text (from Step 4): ஏனெனில் சரியான வழி இழந்திருந்தது. - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): because the right way had been lost - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): for the right way had been missed. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
``` எங்கள் வாழ்க்கையின் பாதையின் நடுவில் நான் ஒரு இருண்ட காடில் என்னை கண்டுபிடித்தேன், ஏனெனில் சரியான வழி இழந்திருந்தது. ```
